relationships.subject: METTL3
relationships.evidence_quote: Methyltransferase METTL3 in non‐alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) could induce the deacetylation of H3K27 and H3K9 by recruiting HDAC1/2 on the CCL2 promoter, thus inhibiting the expression of CCL2 and inhibiting the progression of NASH.

relationships.subject: EZH2
relationships.evidence_quote: EZH2 (H3K27 methyltransferase) could mediate the inhibitory epigenetic modification of H3K27 tri‐methylation of CCL2 and could repress CCL2 expression of macrophages.

relationships.subject: HMGA2
relationships.evidence_quote: HMGA2, a tumour derivative, could up‐regulate the gene transcription of CCL2 in tumour‐associated macrophages (TAMs) by regulating the STAT3 signalling pathway.

relationships.subject: miRNA-325-5p
relationships.evidence_quote: This suppression of miRNA‐325‐5p led to increased expression of CCL2 in the colon‐associated dorsal root ganglion.

relationships.subject: NIS-lncRNAs
relationships.evidence_quote: NIS‐lncRNAs promote CCL2 transcription and trigger neuropathic pain by interacting with DNA/RNA‐binding proteins in DRG neurons.

key_findings: Review of epigenetic regulation of CCL2 via histone modifications, DNA methylation and ncRNA in inflammatory disease.
METTL3 recruits HDAC1/2 to repress CCL2; EZH2-mediated H3K27me3 represses CCL2 in macrophages.
